coconut shell.sustainability_notes: High calorific value; excellent for activated carbon production used in water purification.
coconut shell.risks: Minimal – ensure dry storage to prevent mold.

rice husk.sustainability_notes: Rice husk ash is a pozzolanic material used in green cement to reduce CO2 emissions.
rice husk.risks: Dust inhalation risk during handling – use masks.

banana peel.sustainability_notes: High potassium content makes banana peel ideal compost additive.

food waste.sustainability_notes: Converting food waste to biogas reduces methane emissions from landfill.
food waste.risks: Pathogen risk if not processed promptly. Store separately.

textile waste.sustainability_notes: Textile recycling saves 1.7 kg CO2 per kg of fiber recovered.
textile waste.risks: Chemical dyes may require pre-treatment before recycling.

plastic bottles.sustainability_notes: Recycling 1 tonne of PET saves 1.5 tonnes of CO2 vs virgin plastic.
plastic bottles.risks: Contamination from residual liquids. Rinse before collection.

glass bottles.composition: Silica 70%, soda ash, lime – recyclable indefinitely
glass bottles.sustainability_notes: Glass is 100% recyclable with no quality degradation.
glass bottles.risks: Handle with care – sharp edges. Use gloves.

cardboard.sustainability_notes: Each tonne of recycled cardboard saves 17 trees and 7000 liters of water.
cardboard.risks: Wet cardboard loses value – store dry.

paper waste.composition: Cellulose fiber, wood pulp, bleaching agents
paper waste.sustainability_notes: Recycling 1 tonne of paper saves 1.5 tonnes of CO2 emissions.
paper waste.risks: Confidential documents must be shredded before recycling.

e-waste.composition: Gold, silver, copper, palladium, lead, mercury, cadmium, brominated flame retardants
e-waste.sustainability_notes: E-waste contains 40-50x more gold than gold ore. Proper recycling is critical.
e-waste.risks: CRITICAL: Contains lead, mercury, cadmium – highly toxic. NEVER dispose in regular bins. Causes soil and groundwater contamination. Legal liability under E-Waste Management Rules 2022.

aluminium cans.sustainability_notes: Recycling aluminium uses 95% less energy than virgin production.
aluminium cans.risks: Clean and separate from other metals for maximum value.

steel scrap.sustainability_notes: Recycled steel uses 60% less energy than primary steel production.
steel scrap.risks: Sharp edges. Rust may reduce value.

wood waste.sustainability_notes: Wood waste bioenergy can offset fossil fuel use significantly.
wood waste.risks: Treated or painted wood may contain VOCs – separate before processing.

sawdust.sustainability_notes: Sawdust is excellent substrate for oyster mushroom cultivation.
sawdust.risks: Fine dust – inhalation hazard during handling.

construction debris.composition: Concrete rubble, bricks, tiles, sand, metal rebar
construction debris.sustainability_notes: Recycled concrete aggregate reduces quarrying and carbon footprint.
construction debris.risks: May contain asbestos in old buildings – require testing before disposal.

used cooking oil.composition: Triglycerides, free fatty acids, glycerol – post-frying degraded oil
used cooking oil.sustainability_notes: 1 liter of used cooking oil produces ~0.85 liters of biodiesel.
used cooking oil.risks: NEVER pour down drain – clogs pipes and contaminates waterways. Legal violations under EPR rules.

rubber tyres.composition: Natural rubber 30%, synthetic rubber, carbon black, steel wire
rubber tyres.sustainability_notes: Rubberized asphalt roads last 20% longer than conventional asphalt.
rubber tyres.risks: Open burning of tyres is illegal and causes toxic emissions. Use only authorized recyclers.

coffee grounds.composition: Organic compounds, caffeine residue, nitrogen, phosphorus
coffee grounds.sustainability_notes: Coffee grounds improve soil nitrogen and repel garden pests naturally.
coffee grounds.risks: Avoid large quantities in compost as acidity may harm plants.

sugarcane bagasse.sustainability_notes: Bagasse-based paper uses 60% less water than wood-pulp paper.
sugarcane bagasse.risks: Self-heating possible in large wet piles – ensure proper ventilation.

corn husk.sustainability_notes: Corn husk ethanol has 52% lower lifecycle GHG than gasoline.
corn husk.risks: Store dry to prevent mold formation.

eggshells.sustainability_notes: Crushed eggshells raise soil pH and provide slow-release calcium.
eggshells.risks: Dried eggshells only – fresh shells may attract pests.

fish waste.composition: Fish bones, scales, offal – high nitrogen and omega content
fish waste.sustainability_notes: Fish meal is the highest-protein animal feed ingredient available.
fish waste.risks: Odor management critical – rapid decomposition. Biocontainment required.

leather scraps.composition: Collagen protein, chromium tanning agents (hazardous), dyes
leather scraps.sustainability_notes: Chrome-tanned leather scraps require special handling to prevent heavy metal leaching.
leather scraps.risks: HIGH RISK: Chrome VI in tanning waste is carcinogenic. Requires certified treatment facility. Do not compost.

cotton waste.sustainability_notes: Recycled cotton reduces water usage by 99% vs virgin cotton production.

coconut coir.sustainability_notes: Coir peat is a sustainable alternative to peat moss for horticulture.
coconut coir.risks: Salt content in brown coir may inhibit plant growth – wash before use.

wet waste.composition: Kitchen scraps, vegetable peels, fruit waste, cooked food
wet waste.sustainability_notes: Wet waste to biogas can supply 20-30% of campus kitchen energy.
wet waste.risks: Must be segregated at source. Delays cause leachate and methane emissions.

dry leaves.composition: Cellulose, lignin, trace minerals – organic carbon source
dry leaves.sustainability_notes: Leaf mulch retains soil moisture and suppresses weeds naturally.
dry leaves.risks: Avoid burning – contributes to air pollution and is restricted in urban areas.

garden waste.composition: Mixed green/brown plant matter, prunings, grass clippings
garden waste.sustainability_notes: On-site composting of garden waste creates premium horticultural compost.
garden waste.risks: Diseased plant material should not be composted – dispose separately.

battery waste.composition: Lead acid (lead, sulfuric acid), Li-ion (lithium, cobalt, nickel), alkaline (zinc, manganese)
battery waste.sustainability_notes: Li-ion batteries contain cobalt worth ₹2000-4000/kg – high recovery value.
battery waste.risks: CRITICAL: Lead acid batteries contain corrosive sulfuric acid. Li-ion batteries can self-ignite. Lithium causes chemical burns. NEVER dispose in general waste. Covered under Batteries Management Rules 2022.

medical waste.composition: Sharps, bandages, expired medicines, bodily fluids, pathological waste
buyer_types: CPCB authorized biomedical waste treatment facilities only
medical waste.sustainability_notes: Proper disposal prevents spread of infectious diseases and environmental contamination.
medical waste.risks: CRITICAL BIOHAZARD: Contains pathogens, sharps, toxic chemicals. Governed by Biomedical Waste Management Rules 2016. Mandatory color-coded segregation. Unauthorized disposal is a criminal offence under Environment Protection Act.
